title: AdaServe: SLO-Customized LLM Serving with Fine-Grained Speculative Decoding
technique: SLO-customized speculative decoding: per-request draft token trees chosen by a speculate-select-verify pipeline under a hardware token budget so each request meets its own TPOT SLO

optimized_metrics.evidence: within the context of multi-SLO serving, the primary objectives are SLO attainment.

the goal of multi-SLO serving is twofold: (1) to meet the various TPOT SLO requirements of different requests in the batch and (2) to maximize the number of tokens accepted by the LLM during verification.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: a request is considered to fulfill its SLO if its average per-token latency is no greater than the specified TPOT SLO threshold

optimized_metrics.evidence: this phase aims to maximize overall system throughput.

headline_claim.text: AdaServe reduces SLO violations by up to 4.3× and improves goodput by up to 1.9× compared to the best performing baselines

reported_metrics.where: mean accepted tokens per verification step (ablation)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: SLO attainment is the percentage of requests in a workload that meet their SLO. Specifically, a request is considered to fulfill its SLO if its average per-token latency is no greater than the specified TPOT SLO threshold.
metric_definitions.notes: Attainment uses per-request MEAN per-token latency, not a tail percentile within the request.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Goodput is measured as the number of tokens generated per second for requests that successfully attain their SLO.
l_i + t_spec <= t_i^TPOT * (o_i + acc(T_i)), where l_i denotes the current latency of request r_i starting from the first decoding step, o_i the number of tokens decoded
metric_definitions.notes: Latency counted from first decoding step; prefill/TTFT excluded.

slo_spec: Three categories with TPOT SLOs set relative to a near-zero-load baseline latency: coding 1.2x baseline (aligned with MLPerf 40 ms/token for Llama 70B), chatbot 50 ms/token, summarization 150 ms/token; also SLO-scale sweep and urgent-request proportion sweep
load_regime: Request-rate (RPS) sweep using rescaled real-world trace timestamps, plus sweeps of urgent-request share and SLO scale; synthetic trace
tradeoff_acknowledged: Strict per-request latency favors small batches (lower throughput); AdaServe adjusts speculation depth/width, using shallower trees under heavy load; vLLM-Priority meets tight SLOs only at throughput/other-category cost.
models: Llama3 and Qwen2.5 families (e.g. 70B/32B targets, 1B/0.5B drafts)
workloads: HumanEval (coding), Alpaca (chatbot), CNN/DailyMail (summarization); mixed multi-SLO traces
extractor_notes: Only TPOT SLOs are used; TTFT is not an SLO. Method is lossless (verification) but quality not framed as constraint. Built on FlexFlow Serve; baselines vLLM v0.8.4, Sarathi-Serve, vLLM-Spec(n).
load_class_quote: AdaServe's SLO attainment under increasing request arrival rates (§7.2, Fig 8; rescaled real-world trace timestamps)
